target: WIN-003 detail_evidence: replace the incorrect granite-speed-of-sound passage with air-cavity acoustic mode framing (the actual c3 H1 / c4 H1 finding). Addresses ISS-2366.
kernel_of_truth: Reid (1996-97) genuinely measured a real 117 Hz eigenmode in the King's Chamber sarcophagus. Stone-cavity acoustic eigenmodes ARE a legitimate niche topic in archaeoacoustics, and the dome model is correct that something physical is happening at 117 Hz — it is not a fabricated measurement. Our review is not denying the measurement; we are correcting the explanation. The dome's instinct to attend to this number was not wrong; only the EM-coupling interpretation fails.
why_kernel_doesnt_save_claim: The 117 Hz eigenmode is fully explained by air-cavity acoustics (Helmholtz / room-mode theory, Kinsler et al. Fundamentals of Acoustics ch. 9). The dome model adds no new physical mechanism connecting electromagnetic dome modes to mechanical air-pressure vibrations inside the chamber, supplies no derivation of 117 Hz from disc_radius=20,015 km or firmament_height=9,086 km, and presents no a-priori constraint on which integer harmonic of which base frequency (Schumann 7.83 Hz? Tesla 11.7 Hz? something else?) is the correct comparator. Acknowledging the measurement is real does not validate the harmonic-of-dome-resonance interpretation.
why_c3_H1_carry_over: The granite-speed-of-sound assertion (~5,800–6,000 m/s) in current detail_evidence is dimensionally wrong by ~11× — v_granite/(2L) for L=2.27m predicts ~1,300 Hz, not 117 Hz. The 117 Hz resonance is an air-cavity mode with v_air=343 m/s and wavelength ~2.93 m, mixed-mode across sarcophagus interior dimensions ~2.27 × 0.97 × 0.87 m. The granite walls supply rigid acoustic boundary conditions but are not the resonating medium. This was first flagged by c2-pq4 H1 (2026-04-10), carried as c3 H1 (2026-05-31), and re-flagged as c4 H1 (2026-06-01) — three cycles unfixed.

patches.find_pattern: All three are acoustic eigenmodes determined by chamber/sarcophagus geometry and the speed of sound in granite (~5,800–6,000 m/s) — standard Helmholtz resonance with no electromagnetic component.
patches.replace_pattern: All three are acoustic eigenmodes of the AIR enclosed inside the chamber and sarcophagus, set by interior cavity geometry and the speed of sound in air (~343 m/s at room temperature) — standard cavity acoustics with no electromagnetic component. The granite walls supply rigid acoustic boundary conditions; they do not set the resonant frequency. Were the granite itself the resonator, its sound speed of ~5,900 m/s in the 2.27 m sarcophagus length would predict v/(2L) ≈ 1,300 Hz — about 11× higher than the 117 Hz observation, ruling out granite as the resonating medium. At 117 Hz the wavelength in air is 2.93 m, comparable to combined sarcophagus dimensions (~2.27 × 0.97 × 0.87 m), consistent with a higher-order mixed-axis air mode per Kinsler et al., Fundamentals of Acoustics, ch. 9.

Concedes nothing on the EM-vs-acoustic core argument (which remains intact two paragraphs later: "Acoustic resonance and electromagnetic resonance operate on entirely different physical principles"). Hardens against the precise defender quote-back: "your debunk doesn't even understand which medium is resonating." Adds quantitative air-cavity wavelength check to strengthen the contrast.

anticipated_objections.objection: A dome defender argues: "The whole point of a Helmholtz resonance involves both the air cavity AND the rigid walls — your correction is pedantic since granite walls and air cavity are coupled."
anticipated_objections.response: Coupled, yes, but the resonant frequency in a rigid-walled cavity is set by the speed of sound in the contained fluid (air) and the cavity dimensions — Kinsler et al. Fundamentals of Acoustics §9.2 makes this explicit. The wall material affects damping and quality factor (Q), not f_0. A rigid steel chamber of the same interior geometry would resonate at the same 117 Hz; a granite chamber filled with helium (v=965 m/s) would resonate at ~329 Hz. The frequency is a property of the air mode, not the stone. Identifying the wrong medium is not pedantry; it inverts the physics.

anticipated_objections.objection: A dome defender argues: "117 Hz must come from somewhere; if not granite vibration, why does the dome get no credit for identifying the eigenmode at all?"
anticipated_objections.response: Reid identified the eigenmode in 1996-97. The dome model adopted it ~30 years later as a "prediction" without deriving 117 Hz from dome geometry (disc_radius=20,015 km gives c/(2D) ≈ 7.5 Hz; firmament_height=9,086 km gives c/(2H) ≈ 16.5 Hz; no dome-geometry combination produces 117 Hz — see code_analysis tag derives_from_dome=false). What the dome model contributes is the LABEL "10th harmonic of dome resonance" for an existing measurement, which is the post_hoc=true / relabels_standard=true failure mode this WIN already documents.

anticipated_objections.objection: A dome defender argues piezoelectric coupling: "Granite is quartz-bearing; the air-cavity acoustic mode mechanically stresses the granite walls, which then radiate a piezoelectric EM signal at the same frequency — the EM-acoustic link exists in textbook physics."
anticipated_objections.response: Piezoelectric coupling in quartz-bearing granite is real but vanishingly weak at audio drive levels — electric fields in the µV/m range at the surface of mechanically-stressed granite (Brady & Rowell 1986 on earthquake-light triboelectric emission give the upper bound). Even granting such a pathway, the dome model neither computes the expected EM field amplitude nor measures it. The mechanism is unsubstantiated rather than absent — "we can imagine a coupling" is not the same as "the dome predicts a coupling at strength X and measurement confirms it." The advocate_mode review (c3) preemptively conceded this; nothing in EXP-530 walks that concession back.
